name: Mara
body:
MARA
CR 9

A slim woman rides a sleeping horse which buckles under the woman’s unexpected density.

XP 6,400
NE Medium undead
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +19

DEFENSE

AC 23, touch 13, flat-footed 20 (+3 Dex, +10 natural)
hp 110 (13d8+52)
Fort +8, Ref +9, Will +11
Immune undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +16 (3d6+6/19–20)
Special Attacks crush sleeper
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 13th; concentration +17)

3/day—deep slumber (DC 17), oneiric horror (DC 17)

STATISTICS

Str 22, Dex 17, Con —, Int 11, Wis 17, Cha 18
Base Atk +9; CMB +15; CMD 28
Feats Bludgeoner, Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes, Improved Critical (slam), Lightning Reflexes, Skill Focus (Intimidate), Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Bluff +17, Intimidate +26, Perception +19, Stealth +19
SQ change shape (humanoid, mammal, and bird; polymorph)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Crush Sleeper (Su)

A mara sits on a sleeping creature, which doesn’t initially awaken from the disturbance. For every 10 minutes she spends sitting on the creature, the creature must make a DC 20 Fortitude save. On a failure, the creature takes 1d4 points of Strength damage and 1d4 points of Constitution damage. On a success, the creature can attempt a DC 20 Will save to wake up on a success.

When the creature wakes up, the mara moves to an adjacent unoccupied square as an immediate action. A creature that has taken damage and awakens must succeed at a DC 20 Will save or be affected by the nightmare spell. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

Maras are undead creatures that prey on sleeping animals and humanoids. They prefer to take the forms of ordinary animals, such as dogs, cats, or owls, and follow their intended prey, in the hope their prey will befriend them or, at worst, ignore them. After their prey enters a deep sleep, they return to their humanoid forms, sit on their prey, and then crush the life out of their prey. Their intense weight often leads to troubling dreams but rarely awakens their victims. If interrupted or spotted, maras revert to their animal forms and try to escape, often leaving their prey additionally weary from the dreams they induced.

If maras can’t gently follow their targets into an initially peaceful slumber, they use their spells to force their prey to sleep or make nonlethal attacks to knock out their targets. Against strong resistance, they resort to creating a horrifying waking dreamscape in revenge.

Maras sometimes hire themselves out as assassins and typically only ask for a trinket belonging to their prey as payment. This allays any suspicions about their true reasons for accepting these jobs and allows them to establish a stronger connection with their targets.
